Investment strategy
For Powell Superannuation Fund
hi
September 2019
Fund profile
This document sets out the investment strategy for Pauline Powell Superannuation Fund (the Fund).
J Trustee/s I _Powell Pty Ltd
Member name Date of Birth Superannuation Phase
-Powell 08/10/- Pension
Investment Strategy
The Fund's trustee(s) have agreed on this strategy after considering the following:
• the Fund's investment objectives
• the members' ages, circumstances and retirement needs
• the members are prepared for a moderate to high level of volatility of returns
• appropriate risk management strategies
• diversification and the benefits of investing across a number of asset classes in a long-term investment strategy
• the Fund's ability to pay benefits as its members require (as a lump sum or pension or a combination of both), plus
any other costs that the fund incurs
• the need to balance the members appetite between risk and return
The Trustee has determined to review this investment strategy no less than every year.
General objectives
The primary objective of the Fund is to provide benefits, in accordance with the sole purpose test, for the Fund
members and their dependant at retirement, in the event of death or disablement, or as otherwise allowed under
superannuation legislation. The other key objectives are �o:
• generate total returns from a combination of income and capital growth through investment cycles that are detailed
in the 'investment objectives' section below.
• address the needs of the members for personal insurance cover depending on their individual circumstances and
consider whether that cover may be best owned by the Fund.
Investment objectives
The Trustee(s}, having regard to individual member circumstances including their attitude to risk and return, their
experience, their investment time frame and the Fund's financial state, have established the following investment
objectives for the Fund:
• achieve investment returns {based on market values after taxes and charges} that exceeds CPI by at least 5 per
cent per annum over a rolling 5 year time frame.
• ensure all investments comply with prevailing legislation and the Fund's Trust Deed.
• ensure the Fund has sufficient liquidity to meet expenses and obligations when they are due.
• achieve returns above inflation over the medium to long term.
July2017

Insurance
The Trustee(s) have considered the financial position of the members and their objectives in the event of death or
disability.
For the time being, the level of their financial assets are such, that no personal insurance is required to be held in the
superannuation fund.
Asset allocation
The table below details the strategic asset allocation of the Fund that the Trustee(s) will aim to maintain over the long
term, along with applicable ranges that the Trustee(s) believe are appropriate in order to provide flexibility of decision
making to potentially enhance returns or preserve capital.
The strategic asset allocation is based on consultation with members to determine the most appropriate risk versus
return trade off allowing for their individual circumstances, requirements and return assumptions.

Important note
Certain circumstances may arise that result in the cash allocation of the SMSF temporarily exceeding the maximum
limit and, as a result, the allocation of growth assets temporarily being less than the minimum limit in the table above.
For example, this may be due to recent contributions, or proceeds from the sale of assets, not yet being allocated. In
these circumstances, the allocation of assets must be realigned with the ranges in the table above as soon as
practicable.

In formulating the Investment Strategy, the Trustees have assessed the whole
circumstances of the - Powell Superannuation Fund as required under
section 52B and 52C �uperannuation Industry (Supervision) Act 1993 (SIS
Act) and regulation 4.09 of the Superannuation Industry (Supervision) Regulations
1994, including but not limited to the:
1. risk involved in the investments and the likely return
2. composition of the fund's investment as a whole, including the level of
diversification of investments and any subsequent risk exposure
3. liquidity of the fund's investments having regard to cash flow requirements
4. likely return from the fund's investments having regard to its objectives and its
expected cash flow requirements
5. ability of the fund to satisfy its existing and prospective liabilities
6. trustee duties and powers are performed and exercised in the best interest of
the members and their dependants
7. appropriateness of the member's personal insurance cover.
The investment strategy is to be documented and reviewed regularly.
